body.estimand_functional: \(\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)=\{\gamma_{YT\cdot(D\cup J)}(\Gamma)/\gamma_{TT\cdot(D\cup J)}(\Gamma):J\in\mathcal J\}\), estimated by the simultaneous interval union \(C_N\)

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from one fixed mixed-noise law \(P_X\).
sampling_model.treatment: The coordinate \(T\) is intervened upon in each compatible linear structural model; no treatment assignment is randomized in the observed sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; stability is supplied by \(\lambda I\preceq\Gamma\preceq\Lambda I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Source scales are normalized to unit variance before imposing \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le A_{\max}\), with full-column-rank, sign, and lexicographic loading conventions. The explicitly maintained greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance is recovered from centered empirical characteristic-function moduli on coordinate and pair-sum rays; the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace subclass instead uses clipped fourth cumulants and a global Lipschitz modulus.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 2--4 and \(1\le k\le p\), Theorems 2--3 give at most \(p!\) equivalent mixed-noise SCMs and uniqueness once the causal order is known.
Theorems 5--6 give matching logarithmic minimax rates for latent Gaussian covariance estimation under nonparametric contamination.
The paper gives scalar centered Fourier variance estimation and least-favorable unknown-Gaussian-variance pairs under fixed smoothness envelopes.
The paper constructs test-inversion confidence regions for total effects under structure uncertainty and equal error variances.
The paper gives generic total-effect identification and rigorous confidence regions under structure uncertainty using partial equality restrictions on structural-error variances.
Algorithm 3 unions adjustment-set intervals over retained orders; Lemma 1 gives asymptotic coverage of one effect from order-set and conditional-interval validity.
The paper adapts IDA and joint IDA to maximal PDAGs with background knowledge.
The paper derives estimating equations and asymptotic distributions for fourth-moment ICA procedures.
The paper constructs multiplier-bootstrap uniform deconvolution bands with an unknown error law and an auxiliary error sample.

body.tldr: Under mutually independent, unit-variance, nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable latent sources, a full-column-rank identified loading convention, and an explicitly maintained greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition, a known partial order leaves a finite Cholesky-effect fiber. The project represents that fiber by treatment-predecessor ideals and maps one measurable finite-sample characteristic-function covariance region into simultaneous coverage of every compatible effect without separation at collisions. This guarantee is theorem-level distinct from Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1: their causally sufficient identifiable additive-error model yields asymptotic coverage of one effect after order and adjustment-set inference, whereas the present latent mixed-noise regime is nonnested and receives finite-sample whole-fiber coverage. Expected Hausdorff error is logarithmic on fixed ordinary-smooth envelopes; a matching collision-stratum converse remains conditional on the open smooth-splice construction. Literal standardized-Laplace sources form a root-\(N\) fourth-cumulant boundary.

project_justification.gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi give finite population identification for mixed-noise models, while Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 propagate an asymptotic confidence set for an identifiable additive-error ordering into coverage of one total effect. Neither gives a finite-sample event covering every partial-order-compatible effect after greatest-Gaussian-divisor recovery under latent common sources; the two law classes are nonnested, and the moment-compatible collision lower pair remains open.
project_justification.niche: Fixed-dimensional latent mixed-noise systems with normalized sources, audited ordinary-smooth ray envelopes, an explicit greatest-divisor condition, and genuine partial-order ambiguity require inference for a set-valued effect target rather than selection of an identifiable additive-error order.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the predecessor-ideal functional, an explicit centered ray region with clipping and fallback, a theorem-level nonnesting comparison and finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber guarantee, a conditional route to the fixed-class logarithmic converse, and a literal-Laplace boundary controlled by a global Lipschitz modulus.

body.related_work: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi are the population anchor: their Assumptions 2--4 and Theorems 2--3 use mutually independent nonconstant sources with no Gaussian convolution factor, \(1\le k\le p\), lexicographically ordered loading columns, and full column rank to obtain a finite Cholesky-indexed SCM class. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition here is an additional maintained model condition, not an inherited consequence of that theorem or of the finite-ray envelopes. Wang, Kolar, and Drton study recursive additive-error SEMs \(Z_v=f_v(Z_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})+\epsilon_v\) with mutually independent centered coordinate errors and target settings in which nonlinear functions or linear non-Gaussian errors identify causal order. Their Algorithm 3 unions adjustment-set intervals over orderings retained at level \(1-\alpha/2\), and Lemma 1 derives asymptotic coverage of one total effect from pointwise order-set inclusion and conditional interval validity. It neither supplies finite-sample simultaneous coverage of every member of a partially identified fiber nor recovers a greatest Gaussian divisor. The comparison is nonnested: latent common-source laws in \(\mathcal M\) generically violate their independent-error representation, while their identifiable additive-error class allows laws with ray zeros or without a positive Gaussian divisor, which violate \(\mathcal M\). Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov are the multivariate donor for characteristic-function polarization and logarithmic covariance recovery. Meister is the scalar donor for fixed-envelope centering and Fourier-compensated lower pairs. Strieder and Drton's equal-variance work treats effect size and causal-structure uncertainty jointly. Their 2024 partial-homoscedasticity paper uses equality restrictions among structural-error variances in causally sufficient linear models; it neither identifies a Gaussian convolution divisor under latent non-Gaussian sources nor simultaneously covers the present partial-order Cholesky fiber on collision strata. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis connect background knowledge to IDA effect multisets. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja provide fourth-cumulant estimating equations and pointwise limit theory. Kato and Sasaki give honest Fourier-domain bands with an auxiliary error sample.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The matching lower claim is conditional on completing the uniform Fourier-derivative and weighted-Plancherel estimates for the six-degree smooth Laplace--Student splice. Positivity, full-column-rank membership after unit-variance normalization, the common envelopes, the fixed eighth moment, greatest-divisor status in every direction, and product-experiment indistinguishability must all hold with constants fixed before \(N\) varies. Failure of any one condition removes the matching lower and honest-diameter consequences but leaves the exact fiber and upper confidence construction intact.
body.honest_scope: The exact ideal representation, Lipschitz transfer, finite-sample region, logarithmic upper rate, theorem-level separation from the Wang--Kolar--Drton order-to-effect construction, and uniformly quantified literal-Laplace boundary are theorem targets. The predecessor-ideal representation is a supporting result rather than the field-tier novelty center. The smooth-splice pair and therefore the matching minimax and honest-diameter conclusions are explicitly open; the lower theorem is only the conditional Le Cam implication. The greatest-divisor characterization is an explicit model condition distinct from Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi's primitive source assumptions. Dimension, spectral bounds, loading bound after unit-variance normalization, ray exponents, and envelope constants are fixed and known. The proposal does not claim adaptive unknown-exponent inference, growing-dimension guarantees, polynomial-delay ideal enumeration, correct singleton selection, or minimax sharpness for every exponent profile. Sanity corollary: when \(\preceq\) is a total order, \(\mathcal J\) has one treatment-predecessor ideal and the fiber is the standard singleton regression effect \(\gamma_{YT\cdot D}(\Gamma)/\gamma_{TT\cdot D}(\Gamma)\); with known \(\Gamma\), there is no statistical inflation.
